restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5: caller-visible state is the 17 rate lanes in P0..P3 and R16; capacity A[17..24] is unit-private zero-IV state reinitialized on every PERM5 issue for this single-block absorb-from-IV attack; PERM5 costs 1 unit and deposits L0=A[0]; every other primitive costs 1/1355 units.
Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, prefix rounds 0 through 4, all 256 output bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x) = LE32(x).

Generic van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search on one processor: theta = 2^-32 via L0 < 2^32, maximum chain length 2^40, evaluation budget K0 = 65162*2^112, record cap 2^98, main loop unrolled 16 times; each evaluation rewrites four non-message rate words (P1,P2,P3,R16), issues PERM5, and runs a 2-operation DP test; one run with no restart.

Time, memory and preprocessing are worst-case bounds for every run (time at most 2^127.99938, rounded up to 128.000). The success probability of at least 0.39 (exactly bounded below by 0.3900080 under H-RF) holds under the declared random-function heuristic H-RF.

Generic attack with no cryptanalytic improvement claimed. Tightens the prior 128.002 ticket by making capacity unit-private IV (fresh absorb each evaluation), cutting caller pad/state restores from six to four rate writes.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x) = SHA3-256-r5(LE32(x)) on 256-bit words x: whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point it has not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of every value observed so far. This is the standard premise of the van Oorschot-Wiener analysis. It is used only to lower-bound the success probability (Section 6). Output correctness (Section 5) and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds (Sections 4, 7 and 8) are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: The fixed five-round prefix SHA3-256 restricted to 32-byte messages, iterated along pseudo-random chains from uniformly random 256-bit starts. The analysis uses only the chains started before the first contact (expected number below 2^96; at most 2^98 + 2^88 + 1 chains in any run) and at most K0 - 1 + 2^40 < 2^128 main-loop evaluations.
heuristics.extrapolation: We ran the Section 4 algorithm (with n-bit starts, a hash map in place of the trie and no record cap) on output-truncated versions of the real five-round map (n = 24, 32, 40 and 48 bits) and compared it with a keyed 24-round control. These tests are extrapolated to the full 256-bit map. The analytic success bound itself uses only the H-RF statement, not the measured numbers.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is a heuristic model. Supporting experiments are author-run (no experiment manifest). The rate-only / unit-private-capacity ABI and the L0 deposit are review-sensitive; requiring explicit capacity register restores would return two writes per evaluation and raise the scalar toward 128.002.
